M0-NOMINAL.reading: Inside the cavity the field is zero, so the bulk plasma is not tied to field lines; the aft pole of the cavity leaves through the exit with beta far above 1 and the aft share converges with the domain length. The draped field lines still have to reconnect or stretch away behind it, and electrons stay magnetised in the boundary layer (r_Le/L about 1e-5): neither is modelled, so detachment is plausible in the ideal sharp-boundary limit and not demonstrated.

eddy.note: The wall, not the winding, carries the pulse: the windings see an almost steady field (good for AC loss and quench), and the wall takes the transient force and the heat. Bound from the coupled coil response; the real eddy pattern, the 80 K screen and the wall temperature (which sets its resistivity) are not modelled.

hybrid_cost.assumptions: dx = d_i/2 = 0.071 m, 100 particles per cell, about 1 microsecond per particle push per core, 72 bytes per particle

A1.name: Non-axisymmetric magnetic nozzle
A1.topology: The tangential field on a closed diamagnetic cavity is the surface gradient of a potential: it has at least two zeros (a maximum and a minimum, hairy-ball theorem). Every closed cavity leaks at two or more points; an axisymmetric field must put them on the axis, one facing the shield. Sector coils can move the zeros, not remove them.
A1.result: No free side gap: every ray between the shield cone and the exit meets a cryostat or the cage, so a steered leak lands on hardware (a dedicated dump) instead of the shield
A1.cost: A transverse field comparable to the burn-point field over the shield stand-off stores about 3.0 GJ more and puts net torques and unbalanced pulse loads on sector coils; thrust stays symmetric only for paired leaks.
A1.needs: a 3D cavity or hybrid model (gate D21-D)

A2.name: Revised pulse source
A2.reading: Moving the burn point aft or shrinking the pulse changes the shield share only through the ratio of stopping to hardware distance; the forward pole stays. Only a source that sends less energy into the forward pole (an anisotropic target) cuts it by the factor shown. Loading the pulse with inert propellant to direct it (the Orion pulse-unit precedent) lowers the exhaust speed by sqrt(mass ratio); four 0.016 c burns then cost the mission mass ratio shown.

A3.name: Other fusion-propulsion families

rows.name: Pulsed inertial D-3He micro-pulses in a magnetic nozzle (the Vertex)
rows.maturity: target gain and kHz delivery undemonstrated (WL-001, WL-004)
rows.nozzle: open cavity, two poles, pulse loads
rows.mission: the only family here with exhaust of order 1e7 m/s

rows.name: Magneto-inertial: liner-compressed FRC (Fusion Driven Rocket, NASA NIAC 2012-2015)
rows.maturity: subscale liner tests; gain not shown
rows.nozzle: liner plasma as propellant and shield; heavy, slow exhaust

rows.name: Steady FRC with scrape-off-layer propellant (Direct Fusion Drive, PFRC)
rows.maturity: laboratory FRC, no fusion gain; MW-class units
rows.nozzle: steady magnetic nozzle, no pulse loads, cool exhaust
rows.mission: mass ratio exp(96) and 6 orders below the power: excluded

rows.name: Directed pulse unit: target with a propellant/channel layer that turns X-rays and debris into an aft jet
rows.maturity: Orion pulse-unit physics (fission scale); never at micro-pulse scale
rows.nozzle: forward pole starved; X-ray share becomes thrust
rows.mission: exhaust falls with the added mass: see A2 plate rows

A3.reading: The mission needs an exhaust of order 1e7 m/s. Families that thermalise propellant (liner, scrape-off layer) are two to three orders slower and fail the mass ratio; the source change worth studying keeps the fusion products as exhaust and makes the pulse anisotropic without heavy loading.

A4.name: Bounded speculative capability (NON_CANON, not adopted)
A4.proposal: VTX-S6 forward-pole dump: a renewable lithium-film first wall on the shield face that takes the forward-pole plasma and the X-ray load at the heat flux below, every pulse, for the mission. Extends VTX-S3; no field, momentum or energy is created: the energy it takes becomes heat for the lithium loop and radiators.
A4.magnitude: see thermal shield_heat_flux and xray_shield_flux against the 10-20 MW/m2 tungsten class
limits: heat still has to be radiated at 1800 K (ship radiators are about 14 GW)
momentum of the dumped plasma pushes the ship forward (no thrust loss beyond the missing exhaust)

T1.verdict: The heat leaves with the hydrogen, but at a thermal exhaust speed about 1/3000 of the fusion exhaust: carrying the absorbed heat needs a hydrogen flow millions of times the engine propellant flow, which the mission mass cannot pay. At a hydrogen flow equal to the engine flow it recovers kilowatts. Radiator demand is unchanged.

T2.verdict: Conversion makes driver power but rejects the rest at a lower temperature: more radiator area, not less.

decision.direction: Keep the fusion products as exhaust (the only family fast enough for the mission); study pole steering (A1) and an anisotropic source without heavy loading (A2) in a 3D cavity or hybrid model; solve the 20 K eddy heat and the X-ray sky fraction before any coil work.
